4nkjb8fhk70h55nk7hxl.title: Omelette
4nkjb8fhk70h55nk7hxl.health: Eggs are a complete protein and give vitamins B12 and D. Filling for a small portion.
4nkjb8fhk70h55nk7hxl.source: Quickly added from the meal plan.

buckwheat-egg.title: Buckwheat with an egg
buckwheat-egg.done: The water is absorbed and the buckwheat is fluffy.
buckwheat-egg.health: Buckwheat gives fibre, magnesium and iron, and the egg adds protein. A filling meal that keeps you full for a long time.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve under cold water.
Put it in the rice cooker, add water 1:2 (80 g buckwheat to 160 ml water), salt it and switch it on.
When the buckwheat is almost ready, make the egg: fried in a pan for 3–4 minutes over medium heat, or boiled for 7–8 minutes after the water comes to a boil.
Serve the buckwheat with a knob of butter if you like, the egg on top and the tomatoes on the side.
buckwheat-egg.storage: Cooked buckwheat keeps 2–3 days in the fridge, so you can cook enough for 2 lunches at once.
buckwheat-egg.time: ~25 min in the rice cooker, 5 min hands-on
tips: Rinse the buckwheat to remove dust and bitterness.
Don't open the rice cooker while it's cooking, or the buckwheat will cook unevenly.
For a runny yolk, cover the pan with a lid for the last minute: the white will set and the yolk will stay soft.

caesar-tuna.title: Tuna Caesar salad
caesar-tuna.before: Hard-boil the eggs and let them cool (you can do this in advance).
caesar-tuna.health: Tuna and eggs give protein, and tuna also adds some omega-3. The dressing has a lot of mayonnaise, so don't make a bigger portion of it.
caesar-tuna.notes: In the original the dressing is made in a blender; a fork works too, it just takes longer. You can swap the Parmesan for any other hard grated cheese.
caesar-tuna.source: Lifehacker "Caesar with canned tuna". No blender: mix the dressing with a fork. Notes marked "Claude" are my adaptations.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs: lower them into boiling water for 10 minutes, then into cold water for 5 minutes. Peel and cut into quarters.
Dressing: finely grate the Parmesan. Crush the garlic. In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic and Parmesan with a fork until smooth.
Tear the lettuce leaves into large pieces by hand and put them in a large bowl.
Drain the tuna and flake it with a fork. Add it to the lettuce.
If you're using olives, halve them and add them.
Pour over the dressing and toss gently.
Top with the eggs, halved cherry tomatoes and croutons.
caesar-tuna.storage: Dressed salad doesn't keep. The dressing on its own keeps 1–2 days in a jar in the fridge.
tips: Add the croutons and dressing just before eating, or the croutons will go soggy and the leaves will wilt.
Drain the oil or water from the tuna well, or the salad will be watery.
Pat the leaves dry with a towel after washing — dressing won't stick to wet leaves.
Claude: to be gentler on the stomach, replace half the mayonnaise with plain yoghurt and use 1 garlic clove instead of 2–3.

caesar.title: Caesar salad with yoghurt dressing
caesar.done: The chicken is white inside, with no pink.
caesar.health: Chicken and yoghurt give lots of protein. The yoghurt dressing is lighter than a mayonnaise one, and the lettuce adds fibre.
caesar.notes: Use very little garlic: raw garlic can cause heartburn.
caesar.source: A Rutube video: a light yoghurt dressing instead of mayonnaise.
steps: Drizzle the chicken with oil, season with salt and pepper. Fry in a pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes on each side.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then slice it into strips.
Dressing: mix the yoghurt, lemon juice, a little zest and a tiny bit of garlic.
Tear the lettuce leaves by hand.
Put the lettuce, chicken, cheese and croutons in a bowl. Dress just before eating.
caesar.storage: Dressed salad doesn't keep — dress it just before eating.
tips: Dress the salad right before eating: leaves wilt quickly in the dressing and croutons go soggy.
Dry the leaves well after washing — dressing won't stick to wet leaves.
Don't slice the chicken straight from the pan: let it rest for 5 minutes, or the juices will run out and it'll be dry.
Use very little garlic: raw garlic overpowers the taste and can cause heartburn.

charlotte.title: Charlotte (apple sponge cake)
charlotte.before: Cut the apples in advance — that takes the longest. Take the eggs out of the fridge 20–30 minutes before.
charlotte.done: The top is golden and a toothpick from the centre comes out dry, with no sticky batter.
charlotte.health: Apples give fibre and a little vitamin C. There's half the sugar of the original, but it's still a dessert — a slice with your tea.
charlotte.notes: Sugar is reduced to 100 g — it's sweet enough. Fold in the flour without a mixer, or the batter will deflate. Don't put a cold glass dish into a hot oven.
charlotte.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), no fan (Umluft). Middle rack. The time depends on your oven and dish: in a wide dish the layer is thinner and bakes faster.
charlotte.source: Video by Ekaterina Lav (YouTube). My changes: at most 100 g sugar instead of 200 g; apples in layers — inside the batter and on top.
steps: In advance: wash the apples, core them and cut into wedges (~0.5 cm). You don't need to peel them.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat (no fan).
Grease the dish with butter or line the bottom with baking paper.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt: 1 minute with a mixer on medium speed, or 2–3 minutes with a whisk.

Add the sugar (up to 100 g) and vanilla sugar and beat until the mixture turns pale. Mixer: 5–7 minutes on high speed. Without a mixer: 10–12 minutes with a whisk. Check: the trail from the whisk stays on the surface for a couple of seconds.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour with the baking powder (Backpulver).
Add the flour to the eggs in 2–3 batches and fold it in without the mixer — with a spoon or spatula, from the bottom up, just until smooth.
Pour half the batter into the dish and level it. Spread half the apples on top, pressing them lightly into the batter.
Cover the apples with the rest of the batter and spread the remaining apples on top.
Bake at 180 °C for 40–60 minutes on the middle rack — the time depends on your oven and dish. Don't open the door for the first 20 minutes.
Poke the centre with a toothpick or a thin knife. Dry — it's done. Wet — bake a little longer.
Let it cool in the dish for 10–15 minutes, then slice.
charlotte.storage: Cover and keep at room temperature for 1–2 days or in the fridge for up to 3 days. You can freeze it in slices.
tips: Oven door | Don't open it for the first 20 minutes — the cake will sink.
Whisking by hand | Beat the eggs and sugar for a really long time, 10–12 minutes, until pale and fluffy — that's what makes the cake rise.
Flour | Fold it in briefly and gently: long mixing knocks the air out.
Apples | Choose firm, tart ones and don't slice them too thin — soft apples turn to mush.
Soggy bottom | Don't put all the apples on the bottom: they release juice into the lower layer. Layer them — inside the batter and on top.
Dish | Grease it and dust with flour, or line with paper, or the cake will stick.
Dark top, raw middle | Cover with foil and lower the heat to 170 °C.
ing: ≈ ⅛ tsp — as much as you can pick up with three fingers
to grease the bottom and sides · or line the bottom with paper (Backpapier)

cheese-toast.title: Cheese toast
cheese-toast.done: The cheese has melted and the edges of the bread are golden.
cheese-toast.health: Cheese is a source of protein and calcium. Tomato adds freshness and some vitamins.
cheese-toast.ovenNote: Or in a pan under a lid — 2–3 min
steps: If you like, thinly butter the bread.
Put a slice of cheese on each piece, with a slice of tomato under the cheese if you like.
Pan: dry, medium heat, cover with a lid for 2–3 minutes until the cheese melts.
Or the oven: 200 °C, a baking tray with paper, 5–7 minutes.
tips: On high heat the bottom burns before the cheese melts — keep the heat medium and use a lid.
Put the tomato under the cheese, not on top, so the toast doesn't go soggy.
Don't walk away from the oven: toast burns in a minute.

dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.title: Pizza: dough for 3 pizzas, 40 cm (16 inches)
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.before: Get kitchen scales: everything is weighed in grams. There's very little yeast (half a gram, about the tip of a knife), so ideally use scales accurate to 0.1 g or measure carefully by eye. Chill the water: "55" in the source is most likely Fahrenheit, i.e. about 13 °C. Use cold tap water or add a couple of ice cubes. Have a large bowl and cling film or a lid ready.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.done: The dough is ready when it has grown 2–3 times, is soft, airy and bubbly, and stretches easily without tearing. The source doesn't describe the baking.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.health: A long fermentation gives the dough flavour and an airy texture. How healthy the pizza is depends on the toppings: more vegetables is better.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.notes: The source has no baking temperature or time and no sauce or topping recipe — I didn't invent them. All the kneading, folding and resting steps and times (20 min, 30 min, 18–24 h, 1–2 h) are a typical method for this kind of dough and need checking against the video. The water temperature "55 degrees" is almost certainly Fahrenheit (about 13 °C). Weights are in grams, so you need scales. 0.5 g of yeast is very little — that's the corrected amount from the description.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.ovenNote: The source gives no baking temperature or time. For a home oven people usually use the strongest heat (top and bottom or fan), put the tray or stone on the bottom or middle rack and preheat for at least 30 minutes. This is general advice, not from the video.
steps: Pour the water (545 g) into a large bowl. It should be cool, about like cold tap water.
Add the yeast (0.5 g), salt (21 g) and sugar (16 g) to the water. Stir with a fork for 1 minute to dissolve.
Pour in the olive oil (16 g) and stir.
Add both flours (545 g and 295 g). Mix with a spoon or your hand until there's no dry flour left.
Cover the bowl with cling film and leave for 20 minutes.
Wet your hands. Take the edge of the dough, stretch it up and fold it into the centre. Turn the bowl and repeat 6–8 times all the way round. The dough should become more elastic.
Cover the bowl and leave at room temperature. Repeat the folding 2 more times, 30 minutes apart.

Cover the bowl tightly with cling film and leave the dough somewhere warm (about 20 °C) for 18–24 hours. If your kitchen is hot, put the bowl in the fridge. The dough should grow noticeably, become airy, with bubbles on the surface.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide it into 3 equal parts (about 485 g each) with a sharp knife or scraper.
Shape each part into a ball: tuck the edges underneath and roll it on the table under your palm. The top of the ball should be smooth.
Put the balls in containers or on a floured tray, cover and let them rest for another 1–2 hours.
Gently stretch each ball into a circle with your hands. Don't press the edges hard, so they stay airy. Add the toppings and bake.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.storage: Dough balls keep in closed containers in the fridge for 2–3 days. Take them out 1–2 hours before baking so they warm up. Baked pizza is best eaten right away.
dvsicigebj0e68i2aolm.time: About 24 h, of which about 25 min hands-on (the dough needs a long rest)
tips: Too much yeast: the video had a mistake — the correct amount is just 0.5 g. Don't add more, or the dough will over-ferment and rise too fast.
Hot water: the water should be cool (about 13 °C). Warm water speeds up fermentation and spoils the taste and texture.
Not enough resting time: the dough needs at least 18 hours. If you rush it, the pizza will be dense and bland.
Too much flour when stretching: extra flour makes the crust dry and hard. Dust the table very lightly.
Rough handling: don't press the edges or use a rolling pin, or the air will escape and the crust won't be puffy.

golubtsy.title: Lazy cabbage rolls in the oven
golubtsy.done: The sauce is bubbling, the cabbage rolls are soft and not pink inside.
golubtsy.health: Cabbage gives fibre and vitamin C, mince gives protein. Baking in sauce needs less oil than frying.
golubtsy.notes: The Mel recipe uses 250 g of tomato paste — that's a lot; for my husband's stomach 2–3 tbsp and more sour cream is better.
golubtsy.source: Mel recipe (simple sour cream and tomato paste sauce), checked against T—Zh.
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Finely shred the cabbage, pour boiling water over it for 10 minutes, drain and squeeze it out.
Finely chop the onion, coarsely grate the carrot. Fry in oil until soft, ~5 minutes.
Mix the mince, rice, cabbage and the onion with carrot. Season with salt and pepper and mix well.
Shape into patties and coat them in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil for 3 minutes on each side, until browned. They don't need to cook through.
Transfer to a baking dish. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Mix the sour cream with the tomato paste and a little water, and pour over the cabbage rolls.
Bake for 40 minutes.
golubtsy.storage: Fridge 2–3 days; can be frozen in portions.
tips: Always squeeze the cabbage after the boiling water: extra water will make the mince fall apart.
The rice should only be half-cooked: it finishes in the oven, and fully cooked rice turns to mush.
When frying, 3 minutes per side for a crust is enough — don't cook them through in the pan.
The sauce should cover the rolls at least halfway, or the tops will dry out. Add a little water if needed.

gratin.title: Potato gratin (Potato Dauphinoise)
gratin.story: A dish from our trip to France 🇫🇷
gratin.done: A knife goes into the potatoes easily, and the top has a golden crust.
gratin.health: Potatoes give potassium and energy, cheese gives calcium. The dish is filling and fairly rich — good with a light salad.
gratin.notes: Potatoes: look for "vorwiegend festkochend" on the pack — the slices hold their shape but the sauce turns out creamy. "Festkochend" gives neater layers, "mehligkochend" is softer but may fall apart. The steps are still a draft from my notes from France — check them against the video. Classic dauphinoise usually uses cream, milk and garlic, and not always cheese.
gratin.ovenNote: "Not too hot" — that's what my notes from France say
gratin.source: From my notes. Draft: we'll check the recipe before cooking.
steps: Peel the potatoes and slice them into thin rounds.
Layer the slices in a baking dish.
Pour over a mixture of cream cheese (or sour cream) with egg, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake for about 1 hour at 180 °C.
tips: Slice the potatoes evenly thin, 2–3 mm: thick pieces will stay raw.
Don't rinse the sliced potatoes: the starch thickens the sauce.
Don't make the oven too hot: on high heat the cream curdles and the top burns before the potatoes go soft.
Let it stand for 10 minutes after the oven — the sauce will thicken.

kotlety.title: Oven-baked meat patties (kotlety)
kotlety.done: The patties are browned and the juice from the middle is clear, not pink.
kotlety.health: Meat gives protein and iron. In the oven the patties cook with almost no oil, unlike in a pan.
kotlety.source: T—Zh, a tried-and-tested recipe. You can use Oatly instead of milk.
steps: Cut the crust off the bread and soak the crumb in the milk.
Peel the potato and grate it finely.
Finely chop the onion, crush the garlic.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Mix the mince, potato, onion, garlic, egg and bread. Season with salt and pepper and mix well by hand.
With wet hands, shape 12–13 small patties.
Coat them in breadcrumbs and put them on a tray lined with paper.
If you like, put a small piece of butter on each patty (for juiciness).
Bake for 40 minutes.
kotlety.storage: Fridge 2–3 days. Cooked patties can be frozen. Reheat in the oven at 180 °C for 10–15 min under foil.
kotlety.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat, tray lined with paper
tips: Knead the mince well by hand (you can "slap" it against the bowl) — then the patties won't fall apart.
Don't add many eggs: the patties will turn rubbery. One per 500 g is enough.
Chop the onion very finely or grate it — big pieces break the patties.
Shape them with wet hands and make them all the same size — then they'll cook evenly.
If the patties are a bit dry, next time use fattier mince or bake them under a sour cream sauce.

oatmeal.title: Overnight soaked oatmeal
oatmeal.before: The evening before: soak the oats.
oatmeal.done: The porridge is hot and creamy. No need to cook it long: the oats are already soft.
oatmeal.health: Oats are rich in fibre and keep you full for a long time. Banana adds potassium and natural sweetness.
oatmeal.notes: Send me the YouTube video link and I'll add it here.
oatmeal.source: From a YouTube video: the oats are soaked overnight and the porridge turns out creamy.
steps: In the evening: put the oats in a bowl or pan.
Add water so it's 1 cm above the oats.
Cover with a lid or plate and put it in the fridge overnight.
In the morning: transfer to a pan and add Oatly.
Heat for 3–5 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring all the time.
If it's too thick, add a little more Oatly.
Slice the banana on top. Honey if you like (with caramel Oatly you hardly need it).
oatmeal.time: 2 min in the evening + 5 min in the morning
tips: Soak it in the fridge, not on the counter: in the warm the oats can go sour overnight.
In the morning heat it over medium-low heat and stir all the time — porridge burns on the bottom quickly.
If you forgot to soak it in the evening, just cook regular oatmeal, 5–7 minutes.

pancake-bowls.title: Protein pancake bowls
pancake-bowls.done: The top springs back and a skewer comes out dry.
pancake-bowls.health: Greek yoghurt and eggs give lots of protein for breakfast. Berries add vitamins and fibre.
pancake-bowls.notes: No microwave: you can eat them cold or reheat them in the oven.
pancake-bowls.source: YouTube Shorts video. Recipe translated from English.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
In a bowl, mix the yoghurt, eggs, sugar and vanilla.
Add the flour and baking powder and mix until smooth.
Grease 3 glass ramekins with butter and divide the batter between them.
Put the berries on top.
Bake for 20–25 minutes.
pancake-bowls.storage: Fridge 2–3 days. Put a cold glass dish only into a cold oven and heat them up together.
tips: Don't fill the ramekins to the top — the batter rises.
Don't put a cold glass dish into a hot oven: the glass can crack.
Don't overbake: a dry top and a springy centre mean "done" — after that they turn rubbery.
gallery: 2. Batter in the ramekins + berries, before the oven

pangasius.title: Pangasius with lemon
pangasius.before: Thaw the fish in the fridge (not on the counter). Switch on the rice cooker.
pangasius.done: The fish is white, not translucent even in the thickest part, and flakes easily with a fork. If it's still translucent inside, bake for another 3 minutes at a time.
pangasius.health: White fish is light protein with little fat. It bakes with almost no oil.
pangasius.notes: Serve lemon wedges separately so everyone can add as much as they like.
pangasius.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat, middle rack, baking paper
pangasius.source: Checked against HelloFresh and WeightWatchers recipes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Pat the fish dry with a paper towel.
Grate ½ tsp lemon zest (only the yellow part). Cut part of the lemon into thin slices.
Mix the oil, zest, salt and pepper. Rub the fish with it on all sides.
Put the fish on a tray lined with paper, with lemon slices on top.
Bake for 15–20 minutes on the middle rack. First check after 15 minutes.
pangasius.storage: Eat the same day. Don't refreeze thawed fish.
tips: Thaw the fish in the fridge, not in warm water or on the counter.
Always pat the fish dry: wet fish turns out boiled and watery.
Don't overcook: pangasius is delicate and dries out quickly. Check after 15 minutes.
Put the lemon on top rather than pouring juice over in advance: the acid "cooks" the fish and makes it mushy.

peppers.title: Stuffed peppers
peppers.before: Take the chicken and eggs out of the fridge. Start the rice cooker if you want rice on the side.
peppers.done: The egg inside has set and isn't runny. Cut one piece of chicken: it's white inside, not pink. The cheese has melted.
peppers.health: Bell peppers are one of the richest vegetables in vitamin C. Chicken and eggs give protein.
peppers.notes: If the halves wobble, prop them up with balls of foil so the egg doesn't run out.
peppers.ovenNote: The video doesn't say → top and bottom heat, middle rack, tray lined with paper
peppers.source: An Instagram video, "for weight loss". The recipe is as in the video, with the steps written out in detail.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C and let it heat up while you chop.
Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Wash the peppers. Cut each one in half lengthwise, from the stem down. Scoop out the seeds and white membranes with a spoon.
Put the halves on the tray cut side up, like little boats.
Cut the chicken into small cubes, about 1 cm (like a sugar cube). Season with salt and pepper.
Dice the tomatoes small.
Fill each half with chicken, then tomatoes and a little cheese on top. Save a handful of cheese for the end.
Crack 4 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and beat with a fork for about 30 seconds until evenly coloured.
Spoon the egg into each half. Not to the brim, or it will spill.
Put the tray in the oven on the middle rack for 40 minutes.
Take the tray out, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and put it back in the oven for another 5 minutes.
peppers.storage: Fridge, in a container with a lid, 2–3 days. Reheat: 180 °C, 15–20 min under foil. Freezing isn't a good idea: the egg turns watery.
tips: Don't fill the halves to the brim with egg: it rises when baking and spills over.
Cut the chicken small, about 1 cm: big pieces won't cook through in 45 minutes.
Tomatoes release juice: if there are a lot, squeeze the diced tomatoes a little, or the filling will be watery.
If the halves wobble, prop them up with balls of foil — or the egg will run out.

pirozhki-kapusta.title: Baked yeast pirozhki with cabbage
pirozhki-kapusta.before: Warm the water slightly, to ~37 °C. You can make the filling while the dough rises.
pirozhki-kapusta.done: The tops are golden and the bottoms are browned.
pirozhki-kapusta.health: Cabbage gives fibre and vitamin C. The dough is made with water, no milk or eggs, and the pirozhki are baked, not fried.
pirozhki-kapusta.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), middle rack, baking paper. First check after 25 minutes.
pirozhki-kapusta.source: Recipe by UnicornSteak, 1000.menu. I've already made it — the pirozhki turned out well.
steps: Sift the flour and set aside about 50 g — you'll use it later to adjust the dough.
Mix the main flour with salt (1½ tsp), yeast and sugar (1½ tbsp).
Pour in the warm water (~37 °C) and oil, stir with a spoon, then with your hands. Add the reserved flour until the dough stops being very sticky. Knead for 15–20 minutes.
Cover and leave somewhere warm and draught-free for about 1 hour, until the dough has grown 1.5–2 times.

Remove the outer cabbage leaves and finely shred it; dice the onion. Melt the butter in a pan and cook the cabbage with the onion over medium heat without a lid for ~15 minutes, until soft. Add salt (½ tsp) and 1½ tsp sugar. Let it cool completely.
Knock back the dough and let it rise again for ~20 minutes, about 1.5 times.
Divide the dough into equal pieces. Roll each into a circle ~0.5 cm thick, put filling in the centre and pinch the edges tightly.
Put the pirozhki seam side down on a tray lined with baking paper, spaced apart. Brush with egg yolk. Preheat the oven to 180 °C and let the pirozhki stand for 10–15 minutes.
Bake at 180 °C for about 30 minutes, until golden on top.
Serve warm — with sour cream or a knob of butter if you like.
pirozhki-kapusta.storage: At room temperature for up to 3 days. You can freeze the raw shaped pirozhki for up to 1 month and bake them from frozen, adding 5–10 minutes.
tips: Filling | Only completely cooled: hot filling melts the dough and the pirozhki will tear.
Flour | Don't add it all at once: the reserved part is there so the dough doesn't get stiff.
Warm place | The dough rises faster in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Pinching | Pinch the edges tightly and place the pirozhki seam side down — or the filling will leak.
No rolling pin | You can flatten the circle with your palms or a bottle.
Freezing | Raw shaped pirozhki can be frozen and baked straight from the freezer.
ing: 1½ for the dough, ½ for the filling

pirozhki-kartoshka.title: Baked pirozhki with potato
pirozhki-kartoshka.before: Take the milk and eggs out of the fridge in advance. Melt the butter and let it cool. You can make the filling while the dough rises.
pirozhki-kartoshka.done: The pirozhki are evenly golden, browned underneath, and sound hollow when you tap the bottom.
pirozhki-kartoshka.health: Filling and simple: potatoes give potassium and energy. Baked, not fried — less fat.
pirozhki-kartoshka.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), middle rack, baking paper. First check after 20 minutes.
pirozhki-kartoshka.source: A combined recipe: common proportions from six published recipes for baked pirozhki (VkusVill, Lifehacker, Lady Mail.ru, nur.kz). One dough for all fillings.
steps: In a large bowl, mix the warm milk (~37 °C, slightly warmer than your hand) with the yeast and the sugar for the dough. Leave for 10 minutes — foam will appear on top.

Add 1 egg, the melted and cooled butter (50 g) and the salt for the dough, and stir. Add the flour in batches and knead by hand for 7–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your hands.
Cover the bowl with a towel and put it somewhere warm and draught-free for 1–1.5 hours, until the dough has roughly doubled.

Peel the potatoes, cut into quarters and boil in salted water for ~20 minutes, until a knife goes in easily. While they cook, finely chop the onion and fry it in 2 tbsp oil until golden, 7–8 minutes. Drain the potatoes, mash them with 20 g butter, mix with the onion, season with salt and pepper. Let it cool.
Knock back the dough and divide it into 16 pieces (~55 g). Flatten each into a ~10 cm circle, put a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle and pinch the edges tightly.
Put the pirozhki seam side down on a tray lined with baking paper, ~3 cm apart. Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat. Let the pirozhki stand for 15–20 minutes while the oven heats up.
Beat the second egg with 1 tbsp milk and brush the pirozhki with a brush or a spoon.
Bake at 180 °C for 20–25 minutes on the middle rack, until golden.
Cover the pirozhki with a towel for 10 minutes — the crust will soften.
pirozhki-kartoshka.storage: Under a towel for 1–2 days. They freeze well: cool, wrap and keep for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven at 160 °C for ~10 minutes.
tips: Filling | Only completely cooled: hot filling melts the dough and the pirozhki will tear.
Warm place | The dough rises faster in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Pinching | Pinch the edges tightly and place the pirozhki seam side down — or the filling will leak.
No rolling pin | You can flatten the circle with your palms or a bottle.
Browning | The tops brown faster than the bottoms — cover with foil. Pale ones — give them another 3–5 minutes.
ing: + a little for the work surface
melt and cool · 50 g for the dough, 20 g for the filling
1 tsp for the dough, ½ for the filling

pirozhki-myaso.title: Baked pirozhki with meat
pirozhki-myaso.before: Take the milk and eggs out of the fridge in advance. Melt the butter and let it cool. You can make the filling while the dough rises.
pirozhki-myaso.done: The pirozhki are evenly golden, browned underneath, and sound hollow when you tap the bottom.
pirozhki-myaso.health: Mince gives protein and iron. Baked pirozhki are less greasy than fried ones.
pirozhki-myaso.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), middle rack, baking paper. First check after 20 minutes.
pirozhki-myaso.source: A combined recipe: common proportions from six published recipes for baked pirozhki (VkusVill, Lifehacker, Lady Mail.ru, nur.kz). One dough for all fillings.
steps: In a large bowl, mix the warm milk (~37 °C, slightly warmer than your hand) with the yeast and the sugar for the dough. Leave for 10 minutes — foam will appear on top.

Add 1 egg, the melted and cooled butter (50 g) and the salt for the dough, and stir. Add the flour in batches and knead by hand for 7–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your hands.
Cover the bowl with a towel and put it somewhere warm and draught-free for 1–1.5 hours, until the dough has roughly doubled.

Finely chop the onion. Fry it in a pan with 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes over medium heat. Add the mince, break it up with a spatula and fry for 8–10 minutes, until no longer pink. Add salt (½ tsp) and pepper, pour in 3–4 tbsp water and heat for another 2 minutes — this makes the filling juicier. Let it cool.
Knock back the dough and divide it into 16 pieces (~55 g). Flatten each into a ~10 cm circle, put a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle and pinch the edges tightly.
Put the pirozhki seam side down on a tray lined with baking paper, ~3 cm apart. Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat. Let the pirozhki stand for 15–20 minutes while the oven heats up.
Beat the second egg with 1 tbsp milk and brush the pirozhki with a brush or a spoon.
Bake at 180 °C for 20–25 minutes on the middle rack, until golden.
Cover the pirozhki with a towel for 10 minutes — the crust will soften.
pirozhki-myaso.storage: Under a towel for 1–2 days. They freeze well: cool, wrap and keep for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven at 160 °C for ~10 minutes.
tips: Filling | Only completely cooled: hot filling melts the dough and the pirozhki will tear.
Warm place | The dough rises faster in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Pinching | Pinch the edges tightly and place the pirozhki seam side down — or the filling will leak.
No rolling pin | You can flatten the circle with your palms or a bottle.
Browning | The tops brown faster than the bottoms — cover with foil. Pale ones — give them another 3–5 minutes.
ing: + a little for the work surface
1 tsp for the dough, ½ for the filling

pirozhki-yabloki.title: Baked pirozhki with apples
pirozhki-yabloki.before: Take the milk and eggs out of the fridge in advance. Melt the butter and let it cool. You can make the filling while the dough rises.
pirozhki-yabloki.done: The pirozhki are evenly golden, browned underneath, and sound hollow when you tap the bottom.
pirozhki-yabloki.health: Apples add fibre and a little vitamin C. Still, it's a sweet bake — a couple of pirozhki with your tea.
pirozhki-yabloki.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), middle rack, baking paper. First check after 20 minutes.
pirozhki-yabloki.source: A combined recipe: common proportions from six published recipes for baked pirozhki (VkusVill, Lifehacker, Lady Mail.ru, nur.kz). One dough for all fillings.
steps: In a large bowl, mix the warm milk (~37 °C, slightly warmer than your hand) with the yeast and 3 tbsp sugar. Leave for 10 minutes — foam will appear on top.

Add 1 egg, the melted and cooled butter (50 g) and the salt for the dough, and stir. Add the flour in batches and knead by hand for 7–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your hands.
Cover the bowl with a towel and put it somewhere warm and draught-free for 1–1.5 hours, until the dough has roughly doubled.

Peel and core the apples and dice them into ~1 cm cubes. Warm them in a pan with 3 tbsp sugar over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring, until slightly softer but not mushy. Add the cinnamon. If there's a lot of juice, stir in 1 tbsp starch. Let it cool.
Knock back the dough and divide it into 16 pieces (~55 g). Flatten each into a ~10 cm circle, put a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle and pinch the edges tightly.
Put the pirozhki seam side down on a tray lined with baking paper, ~3 cm apart. Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat. Let the pirozhki stand for 15–20 minutes while the oven heats up.
Beat the second egg with 1 tbsp milk and brush the pirozhki with a brush or a spoon.
Bake at 180 °C for 20–25 minutes on the middle rack, until golden.
Cover the pirozhki with a towel for 10 minutes — the crust will soften.
pirozhki-yabloki.storage: Under a towel for 1–2 days. They freeze well: cool, wrap and keep for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven at 160 °C for ~10 minutes.
tips: Filling | Only completely cooled: hot filling melts the dough and the pirozhki will tear.
Warm place | The dough rises faster in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Pinching | Pinch the edges tightly and place the pirozhki seam side down — or the filling will leak.
No rolling pin | You can flatten the circle with your palms or a bottle.
Browning | The tops brown faster than the bottoms — cover with foil. Pale ones — give them another 3–5 minutes.
Apples | Choose firm sweet-and-sour ones: soft varieties turn to purée and leak.
ing: + a little for the work surface
3 for the dough, 3 for the filling

pp-brauni-banan.title: Healthy banana cocoa brownies
pp-brauni-banan.before: Take the eggs out of the fridge 30–40 minutes before. The bananas should be very ripe, with brown spots.
pp-brauni-banan.done: The top is dry to the touch, and a toothpick from the centre comes out with moist crumbs but no runny batter.
pp-brauni-banan.health: No flour or added sugar: the banana gives the sweetness, and cocoa adds some fibre and magnesium. The dark chocolate on top adds fat — it's a dessert, though lighter than a regular brownie.
pp-brauni-banan.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), middle rack, 14–16 cm tin lined with baking paper.
pp-brauni-banan.source: Recipe by Maria, 1000.menu. The original batter is made in a blender — this is a no-blender version.
steps: Take the eggs out of the fridge 30–40 minutes before. Line a 14–16 cm tin with baking paper. Preheat the oven to 170 °C, top and bottom heat.
Peel the ripe bananas and mash them thoroughly with a fork into a purée with hardly any lumps.
Add the eggs and beat with a fork or whisk until smooth. Sift the cocoa and baking powder on top and mix into a smooth, runny batter.
Pour the batter into the tin and level it.
Bake at 170 °C for 40–45 minutes on the middle rack. Don't open the door for the first 20 minutes.
Poke the centre with a toothpick. Moist crumbs are normal for brownies; runny batter — bake a bit longer.
Straight away, scatter pieces of chocolate over the hot brownie, wait 2–3 minutes for them to melt, and spread with a spoon.
Let the brownie cool completely, then take it out of the tin and slice.
pp-brauni-banan.storage: In a closed container at room temperature for up to 2 days, in the fridge for up to 5 days. The author doesn't recommend freezing. You can warm it for 20–30 seconds in the microwave before serving.
tips: Bananas | The riper they are, the sweeter the brownie and the easier they are to mash without a blender.
No blender | If small lumps stay in the purée, there'll be bits of banana in the brownie — that's fine.
Cocoa | Sift it with the baking powder, or dry lumps will stay in the batter.
Tin | In a tin bigger than 16 cm the layer is thinner — check it after about 30 minutes the first time.
Moist centre | A brownie should stay slightly moist inside — don't overbake it.

quiche-lorraine.title: Quiche Lorraine (bacon quiche)
quiche-lorraine.before: Take the pastry out of the fridge 10 minutes before so it doesn't crack.
quiche-lorraine.done: The filling has set and doesn't wobble in the centre, and the top is golden. A knife from the middle comes out clean.
quiche-lorraine.health: Eggs and cheese give protein and calcium. Bacon and crème fraîche make the quiche rich — best as a small portion with salad.
quiche-lorraine.notes: This is a rich dish (bacon + cream): better as an occasional rather than everyday meal, because of my husband's stomach. The Beaufort from my notes is rarely sold at EDEKA — Emmentaler works. Instead of crème fraîche you can use 200 ml cream (Sahne).
quiche-lorraine.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat, BOTTOM rack — so the base bakes through
quiche-lorraine.source: From my notes from France, checked against a lecker.de recipe. Ready-made pastry from the chilled section.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat.
Finely chop the onion.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until crispy. Add the onion and fry for another 2–3 minutes, until soft. Let it cool.
Unroll the pastry with its paper into the tin. Press it onto the bottom and sides and trim the excess.
Prick the base all over with a fork — so the pastry doesn't puff up and absorbs moisture.
Spread the bacon with onion and the cheese over the pastry.
In a bowl, beat the eggs with the crème fraîche, salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg with a fork.
Pour the mixture over the filling.
Bake on the bottom rack for 35–40 minutes. First check after 30 minutes.
quiche-lorraine.storage: Fridge 2–3 days. Reheat in the oven at 160 °C for ~10 min. Can be eaten cold.
tips: Prick the base with a fork and bake on the BOTTOM rack — otherwise the base will be raw and soggy.
Let the bacon and onion cool before putting them on the pastry: hot filling softens it.
The ratio matters: too many eggs — rubbery filling, too few — it won't set. Stick to 4 eggs per 200 g crème fraîche.
Don't overbake: take it out when the edges have set and the centre still wobbles slightly — it'll finish as it cools.

quiche-veggie.title: Vegetable tart with courgette and pepper
quiche-veggie.before: You can cook the vegetables in advance: they need to cool before going on the pastry.
quiche-veggie.done: The filling has set, a knife from the middle comes out clean, and the cheese is golden.
quiche-veggie.health: Courgette and pepper give fibre and vitamins, eggs and cheese give protein.
quiche-veggie.notes: The "tart" in my French notes has no meat or cream. You can use 3 eggs + 200 g Schmand — it'll be lighter.
quiche-veggie.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat, middle rack
quiche-veggie.source: From my notes from France, checked against the REWE "Gemüse-Quiche" recipe. Ready-made pastry.
steps: Slice the courgette into thin rounds and the pepper into thin strips. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
In a pan with 1 tbsp oil, fry the onion and garlic over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add the courgette and pepper and salt them. Cook covered for 5–7 minutes, until softer.
Take off the heat and let cool (as in my notes: hot vegetables make the pastry soggy).
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Roll the pastry into the tin, press it against the sides and prick the base with a fork.
Spread the vegetables over the pastry.
Beat the eggs with the cream, salt and pepper using a fork. Pour over the vegetables, sprinkle with cheese and herbs.
Bake for 30–35 minutes on the middle rack. First check after 25 minutes.
quiche-veggie.storage: Fridge 2–3 days. Reheat in the oven at 160 °C for ~10 min.
tips: Courgette and pepper release a lot of water: always cook them first and let them cool, or the filling won't set and the base will go soggy.
Prick the base with a fork (as in my notes) so the pastry doesn't puff up.
Bake lower — on the middle or bottom rack — so the base bakes through.
Let it stand for 10 minutes before slicing — the filling settles.

smashed-potatoes.title: Smashed potatoes with quark dip
smashed-potatoes.done: The edges are golden brown and crispy. If they're not crispy, switch on the grill briefly at the end and don't walk away.
smashed-potatoes.health: Potatoes in their skins give potassium and fibre. The quark dip adds protein and is lighter than a sour cream one.
smashed-potatoes.notes: 5 minutes before the end you can sprinkle each potato with a pinch of cheese.
smashed-potatoes.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), baking paper
smashed-potatoes.source: A REWE recipe. I made it with quark and cream cheese instead of cream.
steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C, top and bottom heat.
Wash the potatoes — no need to peel. Boil them in salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife goes in easily.
Drain. Wait 2–3 minutes to let the steam out.
Spread the potatoes on a tray lined with baking paper, spaced apart.
Press each potato with the bottom of a glass or pan to ~1.5 cm thick. The edges should crack.
Brush with oil, season with salt and pepper.
Roast for ~30 minutes, first check after 25 minutes.
While the potatoes are in the oven, mix the quark with the cream or cream cheese until smooth. Add a little zest, lemon juice (start with 1 tbsp), salt, pepper, garlic and herbs.
Serving: dip on the plate, potatoes on top.
smashed-potatoes.storage: Potatoes: fridge 2–3 days, reheat in the oven at 200 °C for ~10 min. Dip: in a closed jar, 1–2 days. Don't freeze.
tips: Let the boiled potatoes dry for 2–3 minutes: wet ones won't get crispy.
Don't smash them too thin: under 1 cm they tear and dry out.
Space them out: crowded together they steam instead of roasting.
The oven should be hot (220 °C) before the tray goes in.
ing: for the water and on top

sushi-cake.title: Sushi cake
sushi-cake.before: Cook the rice according to the packet and let it cool completely.
sushi-cake.health: Salmon gives protein and omega-3, avocado gives healthy fats, nori gives iodine. Smoked salmon is quite salty.
sushi-cake.notes: Sriracha is spicy. Better to serve the sauce separately for my husband.
sushi-cake.source: An Instagram video. Recipe translated from Dutch.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet and let it cool.
Line a glass dish with cling film, leaving plenty hanging over the edges.
First layer on the bottom: smoked salmon.
Add a layer of rice on top and press it down with a spoon. Cover with a sheet of nori and spread it with cream cheese.
Cut the cucumber into thin strips or rounds and lay them out. Thin slices of avocado on top.
Another sheet of nori, then a layer of rice, and finish with the last sheet of nori.
Cover the dish with a large plate or board and flip it over. Remove the dish and the film.
Cut into equal pieces with a sharp knife. A slightly wet knife cuts more easily.
On top: sriracha mayo, spring onion, crispy fried onion, white and black sesame seeds.
Serve with soy sauce.
sushi-cake.storage: Best eaten the same day, the next day at the latest: the rice hardens in the fridge.
tips: Sushi rice must cool completely: warm rice makes the nori soggy.
Not rinsing the rice is the main mistake: unrinsed, it turns into a sticky mush. Rinse until the water is almost clear.
Press each layer down with a spoon, or the cake will fall apart when you flip it.
Cut with a sharp wet knife, wiping it after each cut.

syrniki.title: Syrniki (cottage cheese pancakes)
syrniki.before: If you're using Speisequark instead of tvorog, drain it overnight in the fridge in a sieve lined with a towel.
syrniki.done: Golden on both sides and not raw inside.
syrniki.health: Tvorog gives lots of protein and calcium. Fry in a little oil so the syrniki aren't greasy.
syrniki.notes: Without raisins you can add more sugar.
steps: If you have raisins, pour boiling water over them for 10 minutes and drain.
Mix the tvorog, eggs, sugar, vanilla sugar and salt with a fork.
Add the flour and raisins and mix. The dough shouldn't stick to wet hands.
Shape small patties and coat them in flour.
Fry in a pan with 1 tbsp oil for 3–4 minutes on each side over medium-low heat.
syrniki.storage: Fridge 2–3 days. Reheat in a dry pan under a lid.
tips: German quark is wet: always drain it through a towel, or the syrniki will spread.
Add the flour gradually, until the dough doesn't stick to wet hands. Too much flour makes the syrniki rubbery and floury.
Fry over medium-low heat: on high heat they burn outside and stay raw inside.
Too much sugar also makes them burn — don't add more than the recipe says.
If they're browned outside but raw inside, cover with a lid for 2–3 minutes or finish in the oven at 180 °C for 5–7 minutes.
gallery: 1. Tvorog, eggs and sugar in a bowl

tuna-wraps.title: Tuna wraps
tuna-wraps.done: Golden stripes, and the seam has "sealed" and doesn't unroll.
tuna-wraps.health: Tuna gives protein. Quark instead of mayonnaise makes the sauce lighter, and the vegetables add freshness and fibre.
tuna-wraps.source: Our quick dinner from what's at home.
steps: Sauce: mix the quark with the ketchup.
Drain the tuna. Finely chop the gherkins and mix with the tuna and 1 tbsp of the sauce.
Cut the cucumber into thin sticks and the tomato into thin slices.
On the tortilla: a strip of sauce down the middle, lettuce, tuna, cucumber, tomato, cheese.
Fold up the bottom, then the sides, and roll up tightly.
Dry pan, medium heat: 1–2 minutes seam side down, then 1 minute on the other side.
tips: Drain the tuna well — or the tortilla will go soggy.
Don't overfill: the wrap won't roll and will tear.
Fry seam side down — the seam "seals" and the wrap won't unroll.
You can warm the tortilla for 10 seconds in a dry pan before filling: a warm one doesn't crack when rolled.

ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.title: Charlotte (copy)
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.before: Cut the apples in advance — that takes the longest. Take the eggs out of the fridge 20–30 minutes before.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.done: The top is golden and a toothpick from the centre comes out dry, with no sticky batter.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.health: Apples give fibre and a little vitamin C. There's half the sugar of the original, but it's still a dessert — a slice with your tea.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.notes: Sugar is reduced to 100 g — it's sweet enough. Fold in the flour without a mixer, or the batter will deflate. Don't put a cold glass dish into a hot oven.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.ovenNote: Top and bottom heat (Ober-/Unterhitze), no fan (Umluft). Middle rack. The time depends on your oven and dish: in a wide dish the layer is thinner and bakes faster.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.source: Video by Ekaterina Lav (YouTube). My changes: at most 100 g sugar instead of 200 g; apples in layers — inside the batter and on top.
steps: In advance: wash the apples, core them and cut into wedges (~0.5 cm). You don't need to peel them.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, top and bottom heat (no fan).
Grease the dish with butter or line the bottom with baking paper.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt: 1 minute with a mixer on medium speed, or 2–3 minutes with a whisk.

Add the sugar (up to 100 g) and vanilla sugar and beat until the mixture turns pale. Mixer: 5–7 minutes on high speed. Without a mixer: 10–12 minutes with a whisk. Check: the trail from the whisk stays on the surface for a couple of seconds.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour with the baking powder (Backpulver).
Add the flour to the eggs in 2–3 batches and fold it in without the mixer — with a spoon or spatula, from the bottom up, just until smooth.
Pour half the batter into the dish and level it. Spread half the apples on top, pressing them lightly into the batter.
Cover the apples with the rest of the batter and spread the remaining apples on top.
Bake at 180 °C for 40–60 minutes on the middle rack — the time depends on your oven and dish. Don't open the door for the first 20 minutes.
Poke the centre with a toothpick or a thin knife. Dry — it's done. Wet — bake a little longer.
Let it cool in the dish for 10–15 minutes, then slice.
ymfruz5i6m6i4u3uipfs.storage: Cover and keep at room temperature for 1–2 days or in the fridge for up to 3 days. You can freeze it in slices.
tips: Oven door | Don't open it for the first 20 minutes — the cake will sink.
Whisking by hand | Beat the eggs and sugar for a really long time, 10–12 minutes, until pale and fluffy — that's what makes the cake rise.
Flour | Fold it in briefly and gently: long mixing knocks the air out.
Apples | Choose firm, tart ones and don't slice them too thin — soft apples turn to mush.
Soggy bottom | Don't put all the apples on the bottom: they release juice into the lower layer. Layer them — inside the batter and on top.
Dish | Grease it and dust with flour, or line with paper, or the cake will stick.
Dark top, raw middle | Cover with foil and lower the heat to 170 °C.
ing: ≈ ⅛ tsp — as much as you can pick up with three fingers
to grease the bottom and sides · or line the bottom with paper (Backpapier)
